samples.summary: Re-running EVERY red CI run for a SHA erodes the "unforgeable" CI-fix attempt bound in agent-iterate-ci.yml
samples.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:167-174 counts `runs.filter(r => r.conclusion === 'failure').length` over the branch and documents it as an unforgeable bound: "Actions run history is append-only and the agent cannot delete it". But `reRunWorkflow` reuses the run id, so a re-run that goes green REPLACES that run's conclusion — the run stops counting as failed. Before this delta each `@claude rerun` / `@claude loop` invocation re-ran at most one run (`workflow_runs[0]`), so at most one failure could be erased. The new loops (.github/workflows/agent-rerun.yml:203-206, .github/workflows/agent-loop.yml:159-162) re-run every non-success completed run for the head SHA at once, so a single trusted comment on a flaky PR can flip several `failure` runs to `success` and reset `failedCi` well below MAX_ATTEMPTS, letting the CI-fix loop run past the cap it is supposed to self-terminate at. Fix belongs on the new re-run selection (or on making the bound count run ATTEMPTS rather than current conclusions).

samples.summary: Fan-out of re-runs produces N `workflow_run: completed` events, and the CI-fix job's `cancel-in-progress` group now cancels fixers mid-session
samples.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:19-22 triggers on every `CI` `completed` event with conclusion `failure` (gate at :52-56), and its `iterate` job uses `concurrency: agent-iterate-<branch>` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (:96-98). Previously a rerun/loop invocation produced exactly one re-run and therefore one completion event. After this delta both verbs re-run every red run for the SHA, so when two or more of them fail again their completions arrive minutes apart and each new one CANCELS the in-flight fixer — potentially after it has begun (or partially completed) a commit/push, and each cancelled dispatch burns environment/API budget. The same fan-out lands on agent-review-panel.yml's workflow-level `cancel-in-progress: true` group (:115-118), where each re-run completion (run_attempt > 1 → `active`) kills a panel mid-review; that side is at least handled by `close-stuck-checks` (:2244), the fixer side is not.

samples.summary: Design doc still describes `@claude rerun`'s mechanism as re-running "the PR's CI run" (singular)
samples.evidence: docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2800-2802 ("@claude rerun's last act is `reRunWorkflow` on the PR's CI run") and :1274 ("labels the PR agent:managed and re-runs CI") describe the pre-delta single-run behaviour. The verbs now re-run every red run for the head SHA, and that plurality is exactly what the new `ciRunsToRerun` rule and gate 1 depend on; the doc is the reference future readers will use when they next touch this code. Nothing enforces prose accuracy (only backticked paths are checked), so this will drift silently.

samples.summary: Gate 1's run list is a single unpaginated 100-run window over ALL workflows, while the new re-run path paginates every ci.yml run — the two views of "every CI run for this SHA" can disagree
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs:131 and set-state.mjs:226 both fetch `actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>&per_page=100` with no pagination and no workflow filter, then hand the result to `ciConclusion`, which now demands that EVERY CI run be green. The re-run steps added here deliberately `github.paginate(... workflow_id: 'ci.yml', per_page: 100)` because one page is not enough. On a SHA with many workflow runs (the re-run fan-out itself adds panel/iterate/report runs), a red ci.yml run can fall outside the readers' 100-item window and be invisible to gate 1 while the re-run step still acts on it — the two sides of the same invariant are sized differently.

finding.summary: Re-running EVERY red CI run for a SHA erodes the "unforgeable" CI-fix attempt bound in agent-iterate-ci.yml
finding.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:167-174 counts `runs.filter(r => r.conclusion === 'failure').length` over the branch and documents it as an unforgeable bound: "Actions run history is append-only and the agent cannot delete it". But `reRunWorkflow` reuses the run id, so a re-run that goes green REPLACES that run's conclusion — the run stops counting as failed. Before this delta each `@claude rerun` / `@claude loop` invocation re-ran at most one run (`workflow_runs[0]`), so at most one failure could be erased. The new loops (.github/workflows/agent-rerun.yml:203-206, .github/workflows/agent-loop.yml:159-162) re-run every non-success completed run for the head SHA at once, so a single trusted comment on a flaky PR can flip several `failure` runs to `success` and reset `failedCi` well below MAX_ATTEMPTS, letting the CI-fix loop run past the cap it is supposed to self-terminate at. verdict.reason: All three cited sites exist exactly as described. agent-iterate-ci.yml:171-174 counts branch CI runs with `conclusion === 'failure'` and documents it (167-170) as an unforgeable append-only attempt bound feeding the MAX_ATTEMPTS paging at :217 and the proceed decision at :233. agent-rerun.yml:199-207 and agent-loop.yml:155-163 now re-run EVERY completed non-success run for pr.head.sha via `reRunWorkflow({ run_id: run.id })`, which adds an attempt to the same run id — so a green re-run replaces that run's conclusion and it stops counting toward failedCi at agent-iterate-ci.yml:174. The repo's own mirrored helper scripts/agent/checks.mjs:121-125 encodes the same fan-out rule, and its doc comment (checks.mjs:96-101) states multiple CI runs per head SHA are a real observed condition, so more than one `failure` per SHA is reachable. agent-rerun.yml:223-225 explicitly asserts to the human that the CI-fix attempt bound is NOT reset, which the step above it can now falsify by several runs at once. Maintainer-only gating (agent-rerun.yml:29,74-85; agent-loop.yml:26,62-73) prevents agent self-forgery but does not make the erosion unreachable — an ordinary maintainer invocation on a flaky PR triggers it — so it is not `already-guarded`. This is an invariant another (undiffed) module relies on, violated where that module reads it: in-lane and major under the blast-radius rubric.

finding.summary: Fan-out of re-runs produces N `workflow_run: completed` events, and the CI-fix job's `cancel-in-progress` group now cancels fixers mid-session
finding.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:19-22 triggers on every `CI` `completed` event with conclusion `failure` (gate at :52-56), and its `iterate` job uses `concurrency: agent-iterate-<branch>` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (:96-98). Previously a rerun/loop invocation produced exactly one re-run and therefore one completion event. After this delta both verbs re-run every red run for the SHA, so when two or more of them fail again their completions arrive minutes apart and each new one CANCELS the in-flight fixer — potentially after it has begun (or partially completed) a commit/push, and each cancelled dispatch burns environment/API budget. The same fan-out lands on agent-review-panel.yml's workflow-level `cancel-in-progress: true` group (:115-118), where each re-run completion (run_attempt > 1 → `active`) kills a panel mid-review; that side is at least handled by `close-stuck-checks` (:2244), the fixer side is not.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. agent-iterate-ci.yml:19-22 triggers on all CI `completed` events; :52-56 admits any run with path==ci.yml and conclusion==failure; :96-98 gives the `iterate` job `concurrency: agent-iterate-<head_branch>` with `cancel-in-progress: true`, keyed on branch alone with no run_attempt/noop partition. The fan-out is real and present in both verbs: agent-rerun.yml:199-207 and agent-loop.yml:155-163 paginate all ci.yml runs for the head SHA, filter to red, and call reRunWorkflow on EVERY one (their own comments state "EVERY red run, not just the newest"), so N red runs now yield N re-runs and N staggered completion events where the prior rule yielded one. Nothing guards the fixer against that: agent-review-panel.yml:115-118 deliberately partitions its concurrency group into noop/active because, per its comment at :100-110, cancel-in-progress "KILLS THE PANEL MID-REVIEW" and "#648 had two fixers on one branch for 21 minutes" - in-repo evidence that multiple completions per branch really occur and that the fixer arm never received the equivalent partition. The attempts guard at agent-iterate-ci.yml:148-234 only bounds attempts; it does not serialize or dedupe events, and the amplified failed-CI count trips MAX_ATTEMPTS=4 sooner. This is an invariant relied on by a file outside the diff, violated where that file reads it - in-lane for blast-radius, and major (fixer cancelled after a possible push and before its set-state/loop-status/metrics steps). No refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: `@claude rerun` and `@claude loop` re-run only the NEWEST CI run for the head SHA, which can no longer clear gate 1 now that EVERY CI run must be green
finding.evidence: .github/workflows/agent-rerun.yml:186-190 (`listWorkflowRuns({ workflow_id: 'ci.yml', head_sha, per_page: 1 })` → `workflow_runs[0]` → `reRunWorkflow`) and the identical block in .github/workflows/agent-loop.yml:142-146. Both are the documented recovery path ("Re-running CI now; the review panel will run again and can promote or fix this PR", agent-rerun.yml:204). Under the old `ciPassed` rule the newest CI run won, so re-running the newest run was sufficient to make gate 1 pass. `ciConclusion` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:84-90) now requires *every* run of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the SHA to have concluded `success`. ci.yml has no `concurrency:` block and `pull_request` fires on `reopened`, so a SHA can legitimately carry two runs (e.g. a flaky red run, then a fresh run after a close/reopen, or a manually cancelled run). Once an older run for the head SHA is red/cancelled, re-running only `workflow_runs[0]` leaves it red forever: gate 1 becomes permanently unsatisfiable for that SHA, `mark-ready` exits 1 on every round, and both commands still tell the human the panel "can promote". The fix belongs at these two call sites (re-run every non-success CI run for the SHA, i.e. iterate over `ciRunsFor`), not necessarily on the new rule.

verdict.reason: The finding claims both `@claude rerun` and `@claude loop` re-run only the newest CI run via `listWorkflowRuns({..., per_page: 1})` → `workflow_runs[0]` → `reRunWorkflow`. That code is not present. `.github/workflows/agent-rerun.yml:199-207` paginates all CI runs for the head SHA (`per_page: 100`), filters `completed` runs to those with `conclusion !== 'success'`, and loops `reRunWorkflow` over EVERY red run (falling back to `completed.slice(0,1)` only when all are already green, to emit the `workflow_run` event). `.github/workflows/agent-loop.yml:155-163` contains the identical block. This is exactly the fix the finding requests. The rule is additionally factored and unit-tested as `ciRunsToRerun` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:121-125), whose docblock (checks.mjs:92-119) explicitly records that it is mirrored inline at these two pre-checkout github-script steps and pinned by checks.test.mjs. A repo-wide grep for `reRunWorkflow` shows only these two workflow call sites; all other hits are docs/review artifacts. With every red run re-run, `ciConclusion`'s all-must-be-green rule (checks.mjs:84-89) is not left unsatisfiable by the recovery path, so the described breakage does not exist.
